final_answer:
Let
\[
J_{11}(1)=I+N,\qquad N^{11}=0.
\]
Then
\[
J_{11}(1)\otimes J_{11}(1)=I+U,
\]
where \(U\) acts on
\[
A=\mathbb F_2[x,y]/(x^{11},y^{11})
\]
as multiplication by
\[
u=x+y+xy.
\]
So the Jordan block sizes for eigenvalue \(1\) are the Jordan block sizes of the nilpotent operator “multiply by \(u\)”.

Set \(u=x+y+xy\). Since \(1+x\) is a unit,
\[
y=\frac{u+x}{1+x},
\]
so \(y^{11}=0\) is equivalent to \((x+u)^{11}=0\). Hence
\[
A\simeq \mathbb F_2[u,x]/\bigl(x^{11},(x+u)^{11}\bigr),
\]
with \(u\) acting by multiplication.

Over \(\mathbb F_2\),
\[
(x+u)^{11}=x^{11}+ux^{10}+u^2x^9+u^3x^8+u^8x^3+u^9x^2+u^{10}x+u^{11},
\]
because the nonzero binomial coefficients mod \(2\) occur at \(0,1,2,3,8,9,10,11\).

A Gröbner reduction gives the leading constraints
\[
x^{11},\quad ux^{10},\quad u^4x^8,\quad u^8x^6,\quad u^{16}.
\]
Thus a basis is represented by monomials with caps
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
x\text{-powers} & u\text{-length}\\ \hline
x^0,\dots,x^5 & 16\\
x^6,x^7 & 8\\
x^8,x^9 & 4\\
x^{10} & 1
\end{array}
\]
so the nilpotent Jordan block sizes are
\[
16,16,16,16,16,16,8,8,4,4,1.
\]
These sum to
\[
6\cdot16+2\cdot8+2\cdot4+1=121,
\]
as required.

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
J_{11}(1)\otimes J_{11}(1)
\sim
J_{16}(1)^{\oplus 6}\oplus J_8(1)^{\oplus 2}\oplus J_4(1)^{\oplus 2}\oplus J_1(1)
}
\]
over \(\mathbb F_2\).
